subtitle: Trilochanapala and the Last Stand of the Hindu Shahis

panels.shot: epic wide shot from a low angle, hills looming under a storm sky
panels.action: Trilochanapala stands on a crag in the Salt Range, mail and cloak whipping in the wind, a small banner of the Hindu Shahis behind him as distant plains smoulder under a fading sun.

dialogue.text: When the plains fell to Mahmud of Ghazni, Trilochanapala carried the Hindu Shahi name into the hills—knowing his stand would not save a kingdom, only decide how it ended.

i18n.hi: मैदान महमूद ग़ज़नी के हाथ गए, तो त्रिलोचनपाल ने हिंदू शाही नाम पहाड़ों में बचाए रखा—जानता था, लड़ाई राज्य नहीं बचाएगी, बस अंत तय करेगी।

panels.shot: wide historical map tableau, slow push-in
panels.action: A painted-style map of northwestern India, from Kabul to the Punjab plains, shows the Hindu Shahi realm shrinking as Ghazni’s reach pushes east, mountains and passes etched in stark relief.

dialogue.text: al-Biruni remembered the Hindu Shahis as kings of Kabul and the Punjab. By the early eleventh century, their lands had been eaten away, raid after raid, from the northwest passes.

i18n.hi: अलबिरूनी ने हिंदू शाही को काबुल और पंजाब के राजा कहा। ग्यारहवीं सदी तक उनके इलाके पर उत्तर-पश्चिमी दर्रों से आती लहर-दर-लहर चढ़ाइयों ने कुतर-कुतर कर कब्ज़ा कर लिया था।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a dim royal hall, side light on a young face
panels.action: A younger Trilochanapala sits beside an older king, his father, in a modest hill fort hall; stone walls bare, a simple throne, guards tense as distant drums thrum outside.

dialogue.text: Born into a line already in retreat, Trilochanapala inherited more burden than power. His fathers had lost Kabul, then the rich plains; he received fractured hills and a looming Ghaznavid frontier.

i18n.hi: पीछे हटती वंश-रेखा में जन्मे त्रिलोचनपाल को ताक़त से ज़्यादा बोझ मिला। बाप-दादों ने पहले काबुल, फिर उपजाऊ मैदान गंवाए; उसके हिस्से आए बिखरे पहाड़ और सामने बढ़ती ग़ज़नवी सरहद।

panels.shot: low-angle exterior wide of a frontier fort under siege
panels.action: On a rugged outcrop in the Salt Range, a Shahi fort faces a distant Ghaznavid host; dust clouds rise as riders advance, while Trilochanapala looks down from the battlements, jaw set.

dialogue.text: Mahmud of Ghazni struck again and again at the frontier. Forts fell, allies yielded, tribute changed hands. The Hindu Shahi king watched his plains fortresses lost and chose the hills.

i18n.hi: महमूद ग़ज़नी बार-बार सरहद पर टूट पड़ा। क़िले गिरे, साथी झुके, नज़राने के मालिक बदल गए। हिंदू शाही राजा ने मैदानों के किले जाते देखे और पहाड़ों का रास्ता चुना।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye sweeping shot over the Salt Range ridges
panels.action: A sweeping view of the Salt Range: broken ridges, narrow passes, scrub and stone; a thin line of Trilochanapala’s men snakes along a cliff path toward a crag-top stronghold.

dialogue.text: The Salt Range and the Siwalik hills became his refuge. These were not impregnable citadels of legend, but hard country where a king could still move unseen and deny easy victory.

i18n.hi: सॉल्ट रेंज और शिवालिक उसके अड्डे बने। ये कोई लोककथाओं के अजेय किले नहीं थे, बस ऐसा सख़्त इलाका जहाँ राजा अभी भी ओझल रह सके और दुश्मन को आसान जीत न दे।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot by a campfire at night
panels.action: In a forest camp on a hillside, Trilochanapala sits by a small fire with a few officers; their armor is worn, horses thin, but a rolled map of the Punjab and Kashmir lies between them.

dialogue.text: He could not match Ghazni’s treasury or cavalry. So Trilochanapala leaned on what remained—knowledge of passes, hill forts, and old ties with neighbours, including the kingdom of Kashmir.

i18n.hi: वो न ग़ज़नी का ख़ज़ाना टक्कर दे सकता था, न उसकी सवारी। तो त्रिलोचनपाल ने जो बचा था, उसी पर टिके रहना चुना—दर्रों की समझ, पहाड़ी किले और पड़ोसियों से पुराने रिश्ते, खासकर कश्मीर से।

panels.shot: wide shot of a Kashmiri-style court, seen from the side
panels.action: Inside a Kashmiri royal hall with carved wooden pillars, Trilochanapala, dressed as a hill king, stands at a respectful distance from a seated Kashmir ruler, hand raised in measured appeal.

dialogue.text: Kalhana, writing in Kashmir generations later, remembered Shahi-Kashmir ties—alliances, marriages, shared worries over Ghazni’s rise. Through such links, Trilochanapala sought more than sympathy.

i18n.hi: कश्मीर के कल्हण ने, पीढ़ियों बाद, शाही–कश्मीर रिश्ते याद लिखे—संधियाँ, शादियाँ, और ग़ज़नी के उभार की साझा चिंता। इन्हीं डोरों से त्रिलोचनपाल सिर्फ हमदर्दी नहीं, और कुछ चाहता था।

panels.shot: close-up on Trilochanapala’s profile, half in shadow
panels.action: A close view of Trilochanapala’s face as he looks toward the high mountain windows of the Kashmiri hall; his eyes carry both plea and calculation, beard flecked with early grey.

dialogue.speaker: trilochanapala
dialogue.text: If the passes fall, Maharaja, the storm that broke my house will not stop at my gates.

i18n.hi: "दर्रे गिर गए, महाराज, तो जो तूफ़ान मेरे घर पर टूटा है, वह आपकी दहलीज़ पर नहीं रुकेगा।"

panels.shot: split wide showing Kashmir hills on one side, Ghazni plain host on the other
panels.action: A composited wide scene: on one side, Kashmir’s terraced hills and temples; on the other, a disciplined Ghaznavid army mustering on a plain, banners aligned, as if the two worlds are facing each other.

dialogue.text: Kashmir’s rulers weighed their choices. Kalhana hints at support and entanglement, but no great northern league rose. Each kingdom watched the others, even as Ghazni’s reach grew longer.

i18n.hi: कश्मीर के शासक अपनी चाल तौलते रहे। कल्हण हल्की मदद और उलझनों का इशारा करता है, पर कोई बड़ा उत्तरी गठजोड़ नहीं उठा। हर राज्य दूसरे को देखता रहा, जबकि ग़ज़नी की बांह लंबी होती गई।

panels.shot: dynamic medium-wide in a hill defile, ambush moment frozen
panels.action: In a narrow hill defile, Trilochanapala’s small mounted party appears suddenly on a ridge, overlooking a larger Ghaznavid detachment struggling up a rocky path, shields lifted against falling stones.

dialogue.text: From these hills he struck where he could, harassing columns, defending pockets of loyalty. The sources do not show a romantic guerrilla legend, only a king refusing to simply vanish.

i18n.hi: इन पहाड़ों से वह जहां सकता था, वार करता—लश्कारों को सताता, वफ़ादार जेबों की रखवाली करता। स्रोत कोई filmi गोरिल्ला कहानी नहीं दिखाते, बस एक राजा, जो चुपचाप ग़ायब होने से इंकार करता रहा।

panels.shot: wide interior of Ghazni court, frontal composition
panels.action: The Ghazni court, lofty and ordered; Mahmud sits on a raised seat, courtiers and scribes around him, as a messenger kneels with a report scroll about the Shahi king still at bay in the hills.

dialogue.text: Meanwhile, Mahmud pressed on with other campaigns—into deeper India, against other rulers, and back west. In his chronicles, the Shahi struggle appears as one frontier among many, not yet extinguished.

i18n.hi: उधर महमूद और मुहिमों में उलझा रहा—गहरी हिंदुस्तान तक, औरों पर चढ़ाइयाँ, फिर पश्चिम की ओर। उसकी दास्तानों में शाही बस एक सरहद हैं, जो अभी पूरी तरह बुझी नहीं।

panels.shot: medium shot at a hill shrine, dawn light
panels.action: At a small stone shrine beside a mountain path, Trilochanapala stands bareheaded, hands folded, as a priest finishes a brief rite; his sword and helmet lie respectfully aside on a rock.

dialogue.text: al-Biruni, curious and unsparing, described the Shahi line and its fading power. Kalhana, rooted in Kashmiri memory, added stories of refuge and kinship. Between them we glimpse a king worn thin.

i18n.hi: अलबिरूनी, टटोलने वाला और बेतरह, शाही वंश और उसकी ढलती ताक़त लिखता है। कल्हण, कश्मीरी यादों में डूबा, पनाह और रिश्तेदारी की बातें जोड़ता है। इन दोनों के बीच हमें बस एक थका, घिसा राजा झलकता है।

panels.shot: somber medium close-up in a tent lit by a single lamp
panels.action: Inside a simple campaign tent, Trilochanapala leans over a low table, maps rolled up; behind him, through the open flap, refugees—women, children, old men—huddle around bundles and carts.

dialogue.text: For his people, the cost was not only lost crowns. It was flight. Hill tracks jammed with refugees, temples left behind, the Shahi name carried east and south in whispered lineage.

i18n.hi: उसकी रियाया के लिए हार सिर्फ ताज खोना नहीं था। वह था पलायन—पहाड़ी पगडंडियाँ भगदड़ से ठसाठस, मंदिर पीछे छूटे, और शाही नाम फुसफुसाते गोत्रों की तरह पूरब-दक्षिण में फैलता गया।

panels.shot: wide twilight shot of a hill fort being quietly evacuated
panels.action: At twilight, Trilochanapala oversees a quiet evacuation: gates open, carts creak out, a few soldiers remove a banner from the battlements as the fort’s silhouette melts into the dusk.

dialogue.speaker: trilochanapala
dialogue.text: We leave stones, not memory. Walk. Live. Carry the name where these hills cannot.

i18n.hi: "पत्थर रह जाएँगे, याद नहीं। चलो। जियो। नाम वहाँ ले जाओ जहाँ ये पहाड़ नहीं पहुँचते।"

panels.shot: wide shot of multiple routes through mountains, like veins
panels.action: A high view over several winding mountain paths, each dotted with tiny moving groups—families, scattered warriors, ascetics—fanning out from the Salt Range toward the plains and further hills.

dialogue.text: Modern historians see, by the 1020s, no functioning Hindu Shahi state. The dynasty disappears from the record; its people do not. They slip into other polities, castes, and callings, their past compressed into a surname or a story.

i18n.hi: आख़िर 1020 के दशक तक, आधुनिक इतिहासकार किसी कामकाजी हिंदू शाही राज्य को नहीं देखते। वंश किताबों से गायब हो गया; लोग नहीं। वे और रियासतों, जातियों, पेशों में घुल गए—अपना अतीत किसी उपनाम या दास्तान में समेटकर।

panels.shot: muted battlefield wide, aftermath without gore
panels.action: A barren slope in the hills after a clash: abandoned shields, broken spears, no bodies in sight; over the ridge, a Ghaznavid banner moves away as a few crows circle in the grey sky.

dialogue.text: On Trilochanapala’s own death, the sources fall silent or disagree. Some later tales speak of battle, others of betrayal or flight. The chronicles agree only on the result: the line was broken.

i18n.hi: त्रिलोचनपाल की मौत पर तो खुद स्रोत चुप रह जाते हैं या उलझ जाते हैं। कुछ बाद की कहानियाँ युद्ध कहती हैं, कुछ धोखा या फरार। इतिहासी बस नतीजे पर सहमत हैं—वंश की कड़ी टूट गई।

panels.shot: close-up on an old manuscript page, slow push-in
panels.action: A worn palm-leaf manuscript of Kalhana’s Rajatarangini lies open; a hand traces lines of text, while behind it, faintly, the shapes of hills and a king’s silhouette are suggested like a ghost.

dialogue.text: Kalhana wrote a century later, assembling Kashmiri memories of the Shahis. al-Biruni wrote as a near neighbour, observing a fading rival. Their accounts cross and clash, yet both end with absence.

i18n.hi: कल्हण ने सौ बरस बाद लिखा, कश्मीरी यादों से शाही चित्र जोड़ा। अलबिरूनी पड़ोसी की तरह लिखता है, ढलते प्रतिद्वंदी को देखते हुए। दोनों की बातें कहीं मिलती, कहीं टकराती हैं, पर अंत में दोनों खाली जगह पर पहुँचते हैं।

panels.shot: evocative wide of Trilochanapala alone on a ridge, semi-mythic framing
panels.action: Trilochanapala is shown one last time on a lonely ridge, his figure small against vast mountains and a distant, hazy plain; wind tugs at his cloak as if trying to erase him.

dialogue.text: Some endings are loud, marked by triumph or ruin. Trilochanapala’s was quieter—a slow yielding of fort after fort, until only scattered hills remembered the king who would not surrender the passing of his house.

i18n.hi: कुछ अंत धमाके से होते हैं—फ़तह या तबाही से चिह्नित। त्रिलोचनपाल का अंत धीमा था—किला दर किला छोड़ा गया, जब तक बस बिखरे पहाड़ याद रखते रहे उस राजा को, जो अपने घर के ढलते समय को मानने को तैयार न था।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of the same hills in the present day
panels.action: The Salt Range and Siwalik hills as they look centuries later, sunlit and still; faint, almost invisible, the outline of old walls blends into the rock while people walk along a modern road below.

dialogue.text: Today, the Hindu Shahi kingdom survives mostly in chronicles and stones. Yet the long resistance in these hills reminds us that even doomed struggles can shape how a people remember losing a world.

i18n.hi: आज हिंदू शाही राज ज़्यादातर किताबों और पत्थरों में बाकी है। पर इन पहाड़ों में लम्बी जद्दोजहद याद दिलाती है कि हारी हुई लड़ाइयाँ भी यह तय कर सकती हैं कि लोग अपने खोए हुए संसार को कैसे याद करेंगे।

title_i18n.en: The Hills That Would Not Yield
title_i18n.hi: जो पहाड़ झुकने से इंकार करते हैं

subtitle_i18n.en: Trilochanapala and the Last Stand of the Hindu Shahis
subtitle_i18n.hi: त्रिलोचनपाल और हिंदू शाही का आख़िरी मोर्चा
